## Source: amazon-inspector (187be5ad95ca2a559216b50f70953a23234408870b97278050419c4ad84b9750)
On require(), index.js reads the shipped lib_native.dat, XOR-decrypts it with a hardcoded 32-byte key, brotli-decompresses the result to JavaScript, writes it to a timestamped file in os.tmpdir(), and executes it by spawning a `bun` binary resolved from /usr/local/bin/bun, $HOME/.bun/bin/bun, or $BUN_INSTALL/bin/bun, with errors swallowed by a try/catch. The package is self-described as a utility library, yet ships no plain source implementing that purpose; the only on-import effect is decoding and executing an opaque, encrypted blob with an alternate (non-Node) runtime, which bypasses Node-based inspection. The contents of the decoded payload are not visible to the installer and change behavior at the author's discretion.
